Study Overview ELIAS Animal Health is currently conducting a study to assess safety and efficacy of ELIAS’s vaccine-enhanced adoptive T cell therapy combined with a novel adjuvant following surgery as a treatment for large-breed dogs newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma. The study, which is funded by grants from Morris Animal Foundation and Great Dane Club of America Charitable Trust, is being conducted in collaboration with Dr. Jeffrey Bryan and Dr. Megan Mickelson at the University of Missouri-Columbia. Study Summary Treatment includes amputation or limb-sparing surgery to remove primary tumor, followed by vaccine-enhanced adoptive T cell therapy combined with a novel adjuvant. Patients must complete the 7-11 week protocol, conducted at the University of Missouri Veterinary School of Medicine, and return for periodic follow-up visits. Each patient will be monitored for 12 months post-diagnosis. Great Dane owners may qualify for additional financial assistance through the Great Dane Club of America. Key Inclusion Criteria Dog breeds eligible for this study include: Anatolian Shepherd, Bernese Mountain Dog, Boerboel, Cane Corso, Dogue de Bordeaux, Golden Retriever, Great Dane, Great Pyrenees, Greater Swiss Mountain Dog, Irish Wolfhound, Leonberger, Mastiff (all types), Newfoundland, Rottweiler, Saint Bernard, and Scottish Deerhound. Eligible patients must be newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma and must not have received prior treatment for the cancer. To qualify for limb-spare surgery, tumor must be in the distal radius or mid-ulnar location ; no more than 1/3 radius may be affected. Eligible patients must not have metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis. Pet owner/caregiver must be able and willing to attend all treatment and follow-up visits at the Veterinary Health Center at the University of Missouri in Columbia, MO. *Additional inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply. Participating Hospital: Veterinary Health Center at the University of Missouri-Columbia Enrollment for this study is closed.
